title: जलवायु न्यायलाई प्राथमिकता दिन विश्वसमक्ष पूर्वराष्ट्रपति भण्डारीको जोड
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौँ । पूर्वराष्ट्रपति विद्यादेवी भण्डारीले नेपालका हालैका अकल्पनीय प्राकृतिक विपद्का घटनाले नेपालमा जलवायुको असरको अवस्थालाई पुनः उजागर गरेकाले नेपालको जलवायु न्यायको मागलाई गम्भीर रुपमा लिन विश्व समुदायसमक्ष आग्रह गरेकी छन् । चाइना इन्स्टिच्युट अफ इन्टरनेसनल स्टडिजद्वारा चीनमा आयोजित सन् २०२६ को ग्लोबल गभर्नेन्स फोरम (स्योङआन) सम्मेलनलाई आज सम्बोधन गर्दै उनले नेपालले प्राप्त गर्नुपर्ने जलवायु न्यायको अवस्था दर्शाभएको उनको सचिवालयले जनाएको छ । पूर्वराष्ट्रपति भण्डारीले विश्वव्यापी शासन जलवायु न्यायसँग प्रत्यक्ष रूपमा जोडिएको प्रसङ्ग उल्लेख गर्दै हिमालय क्षेत्रीय जलचक्र, जैविक विविधता र पर्यावरणीय सन्तुलनसँग जोडिएको साझा प्राकृतिक सम्पदा भएको बताइन् । उनले भनिन्, ‘यसको संरक्षण तथा जलवायु परिवर्तनका असर न्यूनीकरण र अनुकूलनका लागि चीन, नेपाल, भारतलगायत हिमाली देशहरूबीच मौसमसम्बन्धी तथ्याङ्क आदानप्रदान, हिमनदी अनुगमन, पूर्वसूचना प्रणाली र विपद् प्रतिकार्यमा सहकार्य विस्तार गर्न आवश्यक छ ।’ उनले संयुक्त राष्ट्रसङ्घीय तथा अन्तरराष्ट्रिय वित्तीय संस्थाहरूको दीर्घकालीन र भरपर्दो सहयोग सुनिश्चित गर्दै जलवायु जोखिम न्यूनीकरणका लागि क्षेत्रीय तथा अन्तरराष्ट्रिय सहकार्य सुदृढ गर्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिइन् । उनले भनिन्, ‘नेपाल यस्तो विश्वव्यवस्थाको पक्षमा छ, जहाँ शक्ति होइन अन्तरराष्ट्रिय कानुनले सम्बन्धलाई निर्देशित गरोस्, सबै राष्ट्रको आवाजको सम्मान होस् र कमजोर तथा जोखिममा रहेका मुलुकका सरोकारले उचित स्थान पाउन् यसका लागि संयुक्त राष्ट्रसङ्घलाई समकालीन विश्वको विविधता र आकाङ्क्षा प्रतिविम्बित गर्ने प्रभावकारी संस्थाका रूपमा सुदृढ बनाउनु आवश्यक छ ।’ शान्ति र विकास एकअर्काका परिपूरक भएको उल्लेख गर्दै पूर्व राष्ट्रपति भण्डारीले गरिबी र भोकमरीको अन्त्य, मानव कल्याणको प्रवर्द्धन तथा हतियारको होडमा खर्च हुने स्रोतसाधनलाई विकासमा परिचालन गर्नु अन्तरराष्ट्रिय समुदायको साझा दायित्व भएको पनि स्पष्ट गरिन् । साथै सम्बोधनका क्रममा उनले समावेशी, उत्थानशील र वातावरणमैत्री विकासका लागि सहकार्यलाई थप प्रभावकारी बनाउनुपर्नेमा पनि जोड दिइन् । उनले भनिन्, ‘गरिबी न्यूनीकरण, गुणस्तरीय शिक्षा तथा स्वास्थ्य, रोजगारी, सामाजिक न्याय र वातावरण संरक्षण अन्तरराष्ट्रिय सहकार्यका प्रमुख प्राथमिकता बन्नुपर्छ ।’ उनले नेपाल–चीन सम्बन्ध प्राचीनकालदेखि नै सांस्कृतिक आदानप्रदान, बौद्ध दर्शन र जनस्तरको आत्मीयताबाट विकसित हुँदै आएको पनि स्पष्ट गरिन् । उनले विश्वमा हाल देखा परिरहेका साझा चुनौतीको समाधान कुनै एक राष्ट्रको प्रयासबाट सम्भव नहुने भन्दै यसका लागि संवाद, सहकार्य र सामूहिक प्रतिबद्धता आवश्यक रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै राष्ट्रसङ्घको बडापत्र, अन्तरराष्ट्रिय कानुन र बहुपक्षीयतामा आधारित विश्वव्यवस्थाले अन्तरराष्ट्रिय शान्ति, सुरक्षा र विकासमा महत्वपूर्ण योगदान गरेको पनि बताइन् । फोरमले विश्वव्यापी शासन प्रणालीलाई अझ न्यायपूर्ण, समावेशी र प्रभावकारी बनाउने दिशामा सार्थक विचारविमर्श अघि बढाउँदै विश्वशान्ति, दिगो विकास र साझा समृद्धिका लागि सहकार्यका नयाँ अवसर सिर्जना गर्ने विश्वास पनि व्यक्त गरिन् । Kathmandu. Former President Bidya Devi Bhandari has urged the world community to take Nepal's demand for climate justice seriously as the recent unimaginable natural disasters in Nepal have once again exposed the state of climate impacts in the country. Addressing the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong'an) Conference organized by the China Institute of International Studies in China today, he outlined the climate justice situation that Nepal needs to achieve, according to his secretariat. Former President Bhandari, citing the context in which global governance is directly linked to climate justice, said that the Himalayas are a shared natural heritage linked to the regional water cycle, biodiversity, and ecological balance. She said, "For its conservation and to mitigate and adapt to the impacts of climate change, it is necessary to expand cooperation in meteorological data exchange, glacier monitoring, early warning systems, and disaster response among Himalayan countries including China, Nepal, and India." She emphasized the need to strengthen regional and international cooperation for climate risk reduction, ensuring long-term and reliable support from the United Nations and international financial institutions. She said, "Nepal is in favor of a world order where international law, not power, guides relations, the voices of all nations are respected, and the concerns of weak and vulnerable countries are given due place. For this, it is necessary to strengthen the United Nations as an effective institution that reflects the diversity and aspirations of the contemporary world." Stating that peace and development are complementary to each other, former President Bhandari also clarified that it is the shared responsibility of the international community to end poverty and hunger, promote human welfare, and mobilize resources spent on the arms race for development. During her address, she also emphasized the need to make cooperation more effective for inclusive, resilient, and environmentally friendly development. She said, "Poverty reduction, quality education and health, employment, social justice, and environmental protection should be the main priorities of international cooperation." She also clarified that Nepal-China relations have been developing since ancient times through cultural exchange, Buddhist philosophy, and people-to-people intimacy. She said that the solution to the common challenges currently emerging in the world cannot be achieved through the efforts of any single nation, and that dialogue, cooperation, and collective commitment are necessary for this, adding that the UN Charter, international law, and a global order based on multilateralism have made significant contributions to international peace, security, and development. She also expressed her belief that the forum will create new opportunities for cooperation for world peace, sustainable development, and shared prosperity by advancing meaningful discussions towards making the global governance system more just, inclusive, and effective.

संस्थाहरूको दीर्घकालीन र भरपर्दो सहयोग सुनिश्चित गर्दै जलवायु जोखिम न्यूनीकरणका लागि क्षेत्रीय तथा अन्तरराष्ट्रिय सहकार्य सुदृढ गर्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिइन् । उनले भनिन्, ‘नेपाल यस्तो विश्वव्यवस्थाको पक्षमा छ, जहाँ शक्ति होइन अन्तरराष्ट्रिय कानुनले सम्बन्धलाई निर्देशित गरोस्, सबै राष्ट्रको आवाजको सम्मान होस् र कमजोर तथा जोखिममा रहेका मुलुकका सरोकारले उचित स्थान पाउन् यसका लागि संयुक्त राष्ट्रसङ्घलाई समकालीन विश्वको विविधता र आकाङ्क्षा प्रतिविम्बित गर्ने प्रभावकारी संस्थाका रूपमा सुदृढ बनाउनु आवश्यक छ ।’ शान्ति र विकास एकअर्काका परिपूरक भएको उल्लेख गर्दै पूर्व राष्ट्रपति भण्डारीले गरिबी र भोकमरीको अन्त्य, मानव कल्याणको प्रवर्द्धन तथा हतियारको होडमा खर्च हुने स्रोतसाधनलाई विकासमा परिचालन गर्नु अन्तरराष्ट्रिय समुदायको साझा दायित्व भएको पनि स्पष्ट गरिन् । साथै सम्बोधनका क्रममा उनले समावेशी, उत्थानशील र वातावरणमैत्री विकासका लागि सहकार्यलाई थप प्रभावकारी बनाउनुपर्नेमा पनि जोड दिइन् । उनले भनिन्, ‘गरिबी न्यूनीकरण, गुणस्तरीय शिक्षा तथा स्वास्थ्य, रोजगारी, सामाजिक न्याय र वातावरण संरक्षण अन्तरराष्ट्रिय सहकार्यका प्रमुख प्राथमिकता बन्नुपर्छ ।’ उनले नेपाल–चीन सम्बन्ध प्राचीनकालदेखि नै सांस्कृतिक आदानप्रदान, बौद्ध दर्शन र जनस्तरको आत्मीयताबाट विकसित हुँदै आएको पनि स्पष्ट गरिन् । उनले विश्वमा हाल देखा परिरहेका साझा चुनौतीको समाधान कुनै एक राष्ट्रको प्रयासबाट सम्भव नहुने भन्दै यसका लागि संवाद, सहकार्य र सामूहिक प्रतिबद्धता आवश्यक रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै राष्ट्रसङ्घको बडापत्र, अन्तरराष्ट्रिय कानुन र बहुपक्षीयतामा आधारित विश्वव्यवस्थाले अन्तरराष्ट्रिय शान्ति, सुरक्षा र विकासमा महत्वपूर्ण योगदान गरेको पनि बताइन् । फोरमले विश्वव्यापी शासन प्रणालीलाई अझ न्यायपूर्ण, समावेशी र प्रभावकारी बनाउने दिशामा सार्थक विचारविमर्श अघि बढाउँदै विश्वशान्ति, दिगो विकास र साझा समृद्धिका लागि सहकार्यका नयाँ अवसर सिर्जना गर्ने विश्वास पनि व्यक्त गरिन् । Kathmandu. Former President Bidya Devi Bhandari has urged the world community to take Nepal's demand for climate justice seriously as the recent unimaginable natural disasters in Nepal have once again exposed the state of climate impacts in the country. Addressing the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong'an) Conference organized by the China Institute of International Studies in China today, he outlined the climate justice situation that Nepal needs to achieve, according to his secretariat. Former President Bhandari, citing the context in which global governance is directly linked to climate justice, said that the Himalayas are a shared natural heritage linked to the regional water cycle, biodiversity, and ecological balance. She said, "For its conservation and to mitigate and adapt to the impacts of climate change, it is necessary to expand cooperation in meteorological data exchange, glacier monitoring, early warning systems, and disaster response among Himalayan countries including China, Nepal, and India." She emphasized the need to strengthen regional and international cooperation for climate risk reduction, ensuring long-term and reliable support from the United Nations and international financial institutions. She said, "Nepal is in favor of a world order where international law, not power, guides relations, the voices of all nations are respected, and the concerns of weak and vulnerable countries are given due place. For this, it is necessary to strengthen the United Nations as an effective institution that reflects the diversity and aspirations of the contemporary world." Stating that peace and development are complementary to each other, former President Bhandari also clarified that it is the shared responsibility of the international community to end poverty and hunger, promote human welfare, and mobilize resources spent on the arms race for development. During her address, she also emphasized the need to make cooperation more effective for inclusive, resilient, and environmentally friendly development. She said, "Poverty reduction, quality education and health, employment, social justice, and environmental protection should be the main priorities of international cooperation." She also clarified that Nepal-China relations have been developing since ancient times through cultural exchange, Buddhist philosophy, and people-to-people intimacy. She said that the solution to the common challenges currently emerging in the world cannot be achieved through the efforts of any single nation, and that dialogue, cooperation, and collective commitment are necessary for this, adding that the UN Charter, international law, and a global order based on multilateralism have made significant contributions to international peace, security, and development. She also expressed her belief that the forum will create new opportunities for cooperation for world peace, sustainable development, and shared prosperity by advancing meaningful discussions towards making the global governance system more just, inclusive, and effective.

Former President Bidya Devi Bhandari has urged the world community to take Nepal's demand for climate justice seriously as the recent unimaginable natural disasters in Nepal have once again exposed the state of climate impacts in the country. Addressing the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong'an) Conference organized by the China Institute of International Studies in China today, he outlined the climate justice situation that Nepal needs to achieve, according to his secretariat. Former President Bhandari, citing the context in which global governance is directly linked to climate justice, said that the Himalayas are a shared natural heritage linked to the regional water cycle, biodiversity, and ecological balance. She said, "For its conservation and to mitigate and adapt to the impacts of climate change, it is necessary to expand cooperation in meteorological data exchange, glacier monitoring, early warning systems, and disaster response among Himalayan countries including China, Nepal, and India." She emphasized the need to strengthen regional and international cooperation for climate risk reduction, ensuring long-term and reliable support from the United Nations and international financial institutions. She said, "Nepal is in favor of a world order where international law, not power, guides relations, the voices of all nations are respected, and the concerns of weak and vulnerable countries are given due place. For this, it is necessary to strengthen the United Nations as an effective institution that reflects the diversity and aspirations of the contemporary world." Stating that peace and development are complementary to each other, former President Bhandari also clarified that it is the shared responsibility of the international community to end poverty and hunger, promote human welfare, and mobilize resources spent on the arms race for development. During her address, she also emphasized the need to make cooperation more effective for inclusive, resilient, and environmentally friendly development. She said, "Poverty reduction, quality education and health, employment, social justice, and environmental protection should be the main priorities of international cooperation." She also clarified that Nepal-China relations have been developing since ancient times through cultural exchange, Buddhist philosophy, and people-to-people intimacy. She said that the solution to the common challenges currently emerging in the world cannot be achieved through the efforts of any single nation, and that dialogue, cooperation, and collective commitment are necessary for this, adding that the UN Charter, international law, and a global order based on multilateralism have made significant contributions to international peace, security, and development. She also expressed her belief that the forum will create new opportunities for cooperation for world peace, sustainable development, and shared prosperity by advancing meaningful discussions towards making the global governance system more just, inclusive, and effective.
